newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 2.319 billion yuan from 1.667 billion yuan with the seven-day contract the most actively traded.
Traders said trading was more active than last Friday with non-banking financial institutions particularly active.
"The brisk domestic A share markets and three new A share issues boosted fund demand from non-banking institutions, in particular securities houses," a trader said.
The Financial News quoted a circular issued by the central bank saying all state banks must do their state debt repurchase business through the interbank trading system from Monday.
Traders said the move would greatly boost trading on the interbank market. Officials declined to give immediate comment.
They said the rates would move narrowly in the near term.
